goal: When a worker starts and a flywheel-owned orphan container left by a prior killed worker is present, the worker's startup reap removes that orphan (the SIGKILL/OOM case the atexit backstop misses) while leaving non-flywheel containers untouched.

relevant: packages/flywheel-container/src/flywheel_container/_docker.py -- the owner marker + selector from container-owner-marker (the scan keys on it); force_remove_container_sync()/remove_container() (lines 367-427) are the removal primitives; the atexit _flush_cleanup_registry (402-427) is the backstop that does NOT run on SIGKILL/OOM, which this startup reap covers.

packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- the worker startup path (around line 2072, alongside the boot retention_sweep) is where the orphan reap runs once on start, before the main loop.

packages/flywheel-worktree/tests/test_orphan_container_reap.py -- new test; stub the docker layer to report a flywheel-owned container present and assert removal is issued, and a non-flywheel container present and assert it is NOT removed.
constraints: Reap ONLY containers carrying the flywheel-owner marker from container-owner-marker (import the shared selector -- do not re-derive the match string); a broad match that removes unrelated containers is a defect.
The reap runs at worker startup (covering the killed-worker case where atexit never ran); it must issue the actual removal for a present orphan, not a no-op.
Must not remove a container a live worker still owns -- target only orphans (e.g. not in the current process's active set); do not change the normal teardown/atexit path.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not redefine the owner marker/selector here -- consume the one from container-owner-marker (the prerequisite).
Do not change git-lease/worktree reconciliation; containers are a separate seam.
Do not modify or weaken existing container or worker tests; do not weaken assertions.
Do not touch flywheel_core purity boundaries.
edge_cases: A non-flywheel / unrelated container reported by the same stub must NOT be removed (no collateral damage).
No orphan present -- the reap is a clean no-op (no error).
The SIGKILL case: atexit never ran, so the orphan is the only signal -- the startup scan must find and remove it.
